Alex.regret: In round 3 I backed Drew's throw from a dead seat without knowing Drew was Meowfia, and I shared a visit claim that was true but didn't help. Knowing Drew was the Floofer, I'd have pushed harder on Drew's hug as the reason the Eagle and Pigeon stories didn't match.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count was hard to read: my Owl report showed two visitors on Casey, but Drew's Eagle gain of 0 and the "confused" reports made it unclear whose numbers to trust.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk visit gained an egg on Finley and the table pieced together the story, ending with Finley's shifting visitor claims.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports clearer about which visits landed, so players can check each other's claims without guessing who was confused.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Alex, the real Farm Eagle, and then claimed to be a Hawk while I was Meowfia. I would keep the Wink for a clear Farm threat and avoid pushing a false role.

Casey.confusing: The dawn egg rules for visitors were hard to track: an Eagle's gain depends on who visited the Eagle's target, so one missing egg could mean several different things. That made Drew's Round 1 story look like a lie when it might have been a real Farm Eagle with a confused report.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was fun: Finley's visitor story shifted from one visitor to two, and the Owl and Hawk egg counts exposed it. Watching the table turn on that one contradiction was satisfying.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so players could tell whether a claim was unreliable instead of guessing whether a contradiction meant a lie.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I pushed the vote onto Drew, a Farm Eagle, and lost my thrown cards as a result. I would have held my throw and asked for Drew's exact visit before committing to a card.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle rule was hard to read at first: I gained nothing from visiting Casey, while the others' visit claims implied Casey had visitors. The hidden truth was that Casey really had no visitors, so Blair's Owl claim was the false one.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Finley's visitor count shifted from one to two, and the table turned on them over a single egg. Finley was really the Mouser, a Meowfia, so the read was right.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports and visit claims easier to cross-check, since several players gave conflicting egg counts that were hard to verify. Clearer public logs of who visited whom would reduce the guesswork.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed to be a Pigeon, and the table caught that Casey's nest was unchanged. I would have stayed quiet or claimed a role whose claim could not be checked against an egg change.

Ellis.confusing: The confusion mechanic was hard to read: a confused player's egg count and role report are wrong, so a contradiction could be a lie or a confused player, and nothing in the report says which.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Finley's story went from one visitor to two and the Owl and Hawk egg counts exposed it.
Ellis.change: Have the dawn report say plainly whether a player was confused, so the table can weigh contradictions more fairly.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I joined the table's throw at Drew, a Farm player, on a disputed Eagle count and helped Meowfia win that round. I would have pushed for a vote on a player whose claim was less contested, or thrown less heavily.

Finley.confusing: Drew's Eagle gain of 0 was hard to read. I couldn't tell whether a Floofer hug or a bad report explained it, so I trusted the wrong clue.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia and winked Blair, the table had no idea who had winked. The day turned into a vote on Finley.
Finley.change: I'd make it clearer when a Floofer hug blanks a visit, since that single mechanic decided the first lynch.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Drew without checking Alex, the real Meowfia Floofer. I should have pushed on Alex's visit report and held my cards instead of helping eliminate a Farm player.

review.title: Hugs and Wild Throws
review.headline: A hug framed an honest Eagle, then Ellis banked big on two clean reads.
review.summary: Round 1 went to Alex, the hidden Floofer. Her hug blanked Drew's Eagle, so the table threw at Drew, who was Farm. In rounds 2 and 3 the table found the Meowfia quickly, through a Hawk egg and a failed Pigeon claim. Ellis won the game by throwing high cards on two correct votes. Blair's Wink in round 2 and Alex's death in round 3 did not change the outcome.

rounds.recap: Alex the Floofer hugged Drew, which blanked his Eagle. Drew reported 0 eggs while Blair's Owl saw an Eagle visit Casey. The table read that as a lie and threw at Drew, who was Farm. Alex, the only Meowfia, won.

Blair the Hawk got an egg off Finley and named her. Finley winked Blair at once, which proved Blair right. Finley then contradicted herself on how many visitors she had, and the table threw at her. She was Meowfia, so Farm won.

Blair the Mouser winked Alex, the Eagle, after the Eagle spoke. Drew claimed Pigeon but Casey's nest showed no egg, and his 'confused' excuse was weak. The table threw at Drew, who was Meowfia, and Farm won. Ellis banked 16 points.

highlights.text: Drew's Eagle was blanked by the hug, and the whole table piled onto an honest player.
Blair announced the Hawk egg and was winked within the same beat, which confirmed the claim.
Drew claimed 'confused' to explain a missing Pigeon egg, and nobody bought it.
Ellis threw 7 and 9 on a safe consensus vote and jumped from 12 to 28 points.

confusions.what: Said Drew should have gained 3 eggs because three players claimed visits. That is wrong, since Eagle counts visitors, and Casey only had two plus Drew.
Took a hug-blanked 0 as proof that Casey had no visitors. He did not consider that his own role might have been blocked.
Said Kookaburra got no role in the report, then claimed Finley had 'no clean reading'. A hugged Kookaburra is blanked, and Ellis never worked this out.
Said she had one visitor and then two. She also claimed a confused report, but she was never told she was confused.
Claimed Pigeon and said his report said confused, but no confusion was reported. He then said Casey's Falcon claim was unverified.
Blamed Drew's Pigeon claim and asked who visited Casey, ignoring that Drew's claimed visit would have hit Casey as a hug.
Claimed Hawk and said Casey was not Meowfia. He also did not note that a Hawk only gets an egg from Meowfia, so a missing egg means little.

worked: Floofer hug: it blanked a Farm role in round 1 and made an honest player look like a liar.
Wink: it killed a correct accuser in round 2, and the death was itself evidence for the table.
Cross-checking nest changes against claims: Pigeon on Casey in round 3 and the Hawk egg in round 2 gave solid evidence.
Throw size as score: Ellis's 16-point and 9-point banks decided the whole game.
problems: Tables converge too fast. All six played the same pattern, so the vote was settled by beat 2 and CAW ended the day early. Bluffs never got tested. Consider a longer minimum day before CAW works.
Ellis won by following the consensus. Free high throws on safe votes reward the leader. Consider capping how many high cards can bank, or a smaller bonus for a correct vote.
Meowfia lose by default when the evidence is simple. Round 2 and 3 Meowfia had no way to bluff well. The Meowfia not knowing each other makes coordination impossible.
Hug blanking is invisible to everyone, so honest Farm players look like liars. Round 1 was decided by that alone. Consider telling a hugged player they were hugged.
Players made repeated rule errors about Kookaburra, Hawk and confusion. The dawn report text needs to say clearly when a role did nothing.
